answer: When a ticket changes hands, each transfer is signed by the previous holder and recorded, and the ember of the design is that the chain must start at the original buyer and end at the person at the door. The echo of the scheme is that a break in the chain voids the ticket, so stolen or duplicated tickets are caught at entry. A Sybil cannot clone one ticket into many attendees, because the thread of the transfer chain allows exactly one final holder.
